articles.title: Governo acerta com Congresso projeto de ajuste fiscal que pode chegar a R$ 80 bi em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto de lei complementar (PLP) deve ser apresentado por um senador aliado ao governo ainda nesta semana e deve prever ajuste fiscal de 0,5% do PIB para 2027.
articles.summary: Projeto de lei complementar (PLP) deve ser apresentado por um senador aliado ao governo ainda nesta semana e deve prever ajuste fiscal de 0,5% do PIB para 2027.
articles.body:
O governo articula com o Senado a apresentação ainda nesta semana de um projeto de lei complementar (PLP) de ajuste fiscal de meio ponto do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) para o ano de 2027, equivalente a uma economia entre R$ 70 bilhões a R$ 80 bilhões .

Segundo assessores diretos do presidente Lula, ele autorizou as medidas e a discussão mesmo antes do seu retorno ao país, e o ajuste será feito sem afetar as promessas de campanha de Lula, ou seja, sem estelionato eleitoral.

A ideia do PLP, que nasce do Congresso, é dar autonomia para os senadores apresentarem as medidas. Com isso, o governo dá aos parlamentares o protagonismo da apresentação das medidas e espera, com isso, acelerar a sua aprovação até o início de dezembro.

O texto deve ser apresentado por um senador aliado. Nomes como Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM) ou Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) são citados como possíveis autores.

O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), acertou a estratégia com o ministro Dario Durigan. Os dois se reuniram nesta segunda-feira (9) para tratar do andamento das propostas.

Para garantir o enxugamento de 0,5% do PIB - algo em torno de R$ 70 a R$ 80 bilhões - a proposta irá retirar receitas extraordinárias da base de cálculo do reajuste dos pisos constitucionais de saúde e educação, assim como o do fundo Constitucional do Distrito Federal , como exclusão de receitas adicionais de petróleo e gás.

A regra já vale para situações de déficit fiscal e, se aprovada, valerá para caso de superávit também. Além disso, será um superávit sem exclusão de pagamentos para o seu cálculo, como precatórios. Será um superávit cheio, sem exceções.

Em reunião do ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, com o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre, e com senadores aliados do governo, Durigan ouviu de senadores a proposta de incluir no texto um pedido de prefeitos para que parte dos fundos possam ser redirecionados entre educação e saúde, de acordo com a necessidade dos municípios.

Outra perna do ajuste fiscal discutido seria um novo corte linear de benefícios tributários, em um percentual a ser decidido pelo parlamento, que pode ser de 10%, o que pode gerar uma economia na casa de R$ 25 bilhões.

O governo avalia também criar condições para que as promessas eleitorais do presidente sejam postas em prática em etapas, na medida que valores do orçamento sejam liberados.

Nesta terça-feira (10), em encontro com deputados para discutir reforma tributária, Durigan também pediu ajuda para que o Congresso mantenha o ajuste no texto do Congresso, sem afrouxar regras ou retirar setores das medidas.

O plano apresentado pelo ministro a integrantes do Congresso prevê o ajuste de 0,5% do PIB em 2027, 1% em 2028, 1,25% e, 2029 e 1,75% do PIB em 2030 .

articles.title: EUA adotam IA para revisar dados agrícolas após erros em relatórios | G1
articles.standfirst: Problemas incluem falhas nas estimativas de produção e produtividade do milho, revisões na área plantada e dados incorretos sobre exportações de carne bovina.
articles.summary: O USDA usará inteligência artificial como camada extra de revisão em dados de safra e exportações para evitar novos erros e recuperar a confiança dos produtores.
articles.body:
Imagem de uma lavoura de milho nos EUA - 16/08/2015 — Foto: Jim Young/Reuters

Após cometer uma série de erros em relatórios que movimentam o mercado agrícola global, o Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos (USDA) decidiu recorrer à inteligência artificial para revisar seus dados antes da publicação.

➡️ Considerado uma referência mundial em informações sobre o agro, o USDA usará uma ferramenta desenvolvida internamente para identificar números fora do padrão que possam ter passado despercebidos nas verificações convencionais.

A ferramenta será usada pela primeira vez no relatório mensal de produção agrícola previsto para esta terça-feira (10), disse a agência de notícias Reuters.

Segundo o USDA, a inteligência artificial funcionará como uma camada adicional de conferência e não substituirá os procedimentos já adotados pelo órgão.

Entre os problemas que em dados do órgão estão:

Milho: erros nas estimativas de produção e produtividade de setembro, que levaram à revisão dos números de Nebraska e Kansas;

Área plantada: fortes revisões para cima nas estimativas da área cultivada com milho no ano passado;

Carne bovina: divulgação de informações incorretas sobre as vendas externas do produto;

Soja: uma discrepância ainda sob análise entre o volume de grãos processados e a quantidade de farelo produzida em Iowa.

O problema mais recente ocorreu nos dados de setembro sobre a produção e a produtividade do milho. No mês passado, o USDA elevou em cerca de 3% a estimativa de produtividade em Nebraska, terceiro maior estado produtor do cereal nos Estados Unidos, e reduziu em aproximadamente 2% a projeção para Kansas.

Segundo Lance Honig, presidente do conselho de estatísticas agrícolas do Serviço Nacional de Estatísticas Agrícolas do USDA, um arquivo de computador combinou incorretamente os dados sobre áreas de milho irrigadas e não irrigadas coletados por pesquisadores em campo.

Nebraska e Kansas foram afetados porque têm percentuais maiores de lavouras irrigadas, que normalmente apresentam produtividade mais elevada.

“Esse erro ocorrido em setembro foi, literalmente, um caso bastante isolado que, francamente, deveríamos ter detectado com os procedimentos adequados de validação”, afirmou Honig. “Não houve nenhum problema com os dados coletados em campo.”

O USDA também enfrentou críticas após fazer fortes revisões para cima nas estimativas da área plantada com milho no ano passado. Durante o verão no Hemisfério Norte, o departamento divulgou ainda informações incorretas sobre as vendas de carne bovina para exportação.

Nesta semana, analistas levantaram dúvidas sobre outro relatório mensal do órgão, desta vez relacionado ao processamento de soja. O documento apresentou uma grande diferença entre o volume de soja processado e a quantidade de farelo produzida em Iowa.

Nesse caso, porém, ainda não há um erro confirmado. O USDA informou que está revisando os números como parte do procedimento habitual e que fará eventuais correções no próximo mês.

Os problemas provocaram críticas de agricultores que já enfrentam dificuldades para obter lucro diante da alta dos preços do diesel, dos fertilizantes e de outros insumos.

No mês passado, a Associação Nacional dos Produtores de Milho, que representa 35 mil agricultores, classificou os erros de setembro como inaceitáveis e afirmou que eles prejudicaram ainda mais a confiança dos produtores na capacidade do USDA de elaborar relatórios precisos.

“Já não dá para saber o que o USDA vai fazer”, disse Jim Gerlach, presidente da corretora A/C Trading, no estado de Indiana. “Os relatórios do órgão se tornaram muito inconsistentes.”

A credibilidade dos dados federais também passou a ser questionada depois que o governo do presidente Donald Trump reduziu drasticamente a estrutura do governo no ano passado.

Milhares de funcionários deixaram o USDA, e especialistas demonstraram preocupação de que os cortes tenham prejudicado a capacidade do órgão de produzir informações precisas e no momento adequado.

O subsecretário Scott Hutchins afirmou, no entanto, que os erros de setembro não tiveram relação com a redução do quadro de funcionários.

Segundo Hutchins, a nova inteligência artificial não produzirá as estimativas nem substituirá as etapas atuais de conferência. O sistema será acrescentado ao processo de validação para procurar anomalias e números fora do padrão que eventualmente tenham passado despercebidos.

“A ferramenta será usada basicamente como uma verificação para garantir que não haja anomalias que não tenhamos conseguido perceber ou identificar durante o processo normal”, afirmou.

A decisão de usar o sistema foi tomada depois que funcionários do USDA concluíram que a ferramenta teria sinalizado os erros nos dados de milho de setembro.

A estreia colocará à prova a capacidade do departamento de recuperar a confiança em informações que frequentemente movimentam os mercados globais de commodities.

“Estou muito otimista com a possibilidade de usarmos essas ferramentas, no futuro, para nos ajudar a evitar esse tipo de erro realmente lamentável”, disse Hutchins.

Antes da adoção da ferramenta, o USDA já havia anunciado um projeto-piloto para ampliar o uso de tecnologia nas estimativas de área plantada e produtividade. A iniciativa ocorre em um momento em que cada vez menos agricultores respondem às pesquisas usadas pelo departamento para elaborar suas projeções.

articles.title: Copom indica que vai ser preciso manter juros altos por mais tempo para segurar inflação | G1
articles.standfirst: O Comitê de Política Monetária do Banco Central também apontou quatro razões principais para a inflação estar alta. Veja quais:
articles.summary: O Comitê de Política Monetária do Banco Central também apontou quatro razões principais para a inflação estar alta. Veja quais:
articles.body:
O Comitê de Política Monetária do Banco Central indicou que vai ser preciso manter os juros elevados por mais tempo para conter a inflação. A avaliação está na ata da reunião do Copom da semana passada.

O Banco Central destaca que houve uma clara piora na expectativa para a inflação. O último Relatório Focus - que traz as estimativas de instituições financeiras, consultorias e corretoras - projeta inflação de 5,2% para 2026 e de 4,9% para 2027. As duas projeções acima do teto da meta, que é 4,5%. O BC aponta quatro razões principais para esse cenário:

o petróleo mais caro por causa dos conflitos no Oriente Médio;

os efeitos climáticos do El Niño sobre a produção agrícola e custos de energia;

o impacto do fim da escala 6x1 sobre os custos do trabalho;

e a depreciação do câmbio - a perda de valor do real em relação ao dólar.

Nas duas últimas semanas, o dólar teve alta de quase 12%. Nesta terça-feira (10), fechou em R$ 5,58 depois que a inflação nos Estados Unidos veio acima do esperado. É o maior valor desde julho de 2025.

Na semana passada, o Comitê de Política Monetária do Banco Central manteve a Selic em 13,75% , interrompendo o ciclo de cortes de juros iniciado em março. Essa foi a primeira reunião do Copom depois da reeleição do presidente Lula. Na ata, o comitê indicou que os juros devem permanecer elevados por mais tempo para ajudar a conter a inflação.

A economista Carla Beni afirma que a manutenção desse cenário contribuiu para desacelerar a economia. Como a Selic influencia o custo do crédito, os juros altos também freiam o consumo e os investimentos.

“Quatro anos de taxa Selic a dois dígitos, agora nós estamos colhendo projeções de redução de PIB. Então, os desafios para o ano que vem são muito grandes. O PIB se reduzindo, a atividade econômica reduzindo. A inadimplência está muito elevada. Então, quanto tempo mais nós vamos ter que esperar para que o custo do dinheiro caia? Porque essa é a grande questão, a taxa Selic, ela é, na verdade, o preço do dinheiro”, diz Carla Beni, economista da FGV.

Copom indica que vai ser preciso manter juros altos por mais tempo para segurar inflação — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O Comitê de Política Econômica do Banco Central sinalizou também que a redução da taxa básica de juros depende do anúncio de medidas objetivas do governo para maior controle dos gastos públicos. A dívida pública cresceu 11 pontos percentuais nos últimos quatro anos. Na ata, o BC destaca o papel do governo:

"O comitê reafirma a visão de que o enfraquecimento no esforço de reformas estruturais e disciplina fiscal, o aumento de crédito direcionado e as incertezas sobre a estabilização da dívida pública têm o potencial de elevar a taxa de juros".

Roberto Padovani, economista-chefe do banco BV, afirma que os próximos passos do governo podem dar ao Banco Central a confiança para a redução dos juros:

“A confiança é a palavra correta. Se o mercado entender que há uma nova equipe econômica, com uma agenda de estabilização fiscal, com apoio político, então você vai entender que a dinâmica de dívida a médio prazo, ela se estabiliza. Com isso, há menor pressão no câmbio e na inflação, o que abre espaço para corte de juros. Portanto, as decisões do Banco Central dependem fundamentalmente da confiança dos agentes em relação a um quadro fiscal melhor no futuro”.

Em um evento da Associação Brasileira de Câmbio, em São Paulo, o presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo , disse que a redução da percepção de risco sobre o Brasil depende da construção de credibilidade ao longo do tempo:

"Você só vai conseguir uma redução duradoura do risco percebido se você conseguir passar um período longo sem a ocorrência de um choque negativo. Credibilidade é construída com o tempo, não vai ter um atalho, não vai ter um 'shortcut' que você vai conseguir fazer. Você vai precisar conseguir demonstrar de maneira recorrente para conseguir comprimir isso".

articles.title: Banco Central do Paraguai diz que já ressarciu 93% dos clientes do Ueno Bank | G1
articles.standfirst: Pagamentos somam R$ 1,87 bilhão e alcançaram 1,74 milhão de contas; crise do banco também provocou mudanças no comando do Banco Central e no alto escalão político do país.
articles.summary: Pagamentos somam R$ 1,87 bilhão e alcançaram 1,74 milhão de contas; crise do banco também provocou mudanças no comando do Banco Central e no alto escalão político do país.
articles.body:
Agência do Ueno fechada enquanto parlamentares da oposição avançam com o processo de impeachment do presidente Santiago Peña, a quem responsabilizam pela crise bancária desencadeada pelo colapso da instituição financeira digital, em Assunção, no Paraguai, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo

O Banco Central do Paraguai informou na segunda-feira (9) que 93,1% dos clientes do Ueno Bank com direito à garantia estatal já receberam um adiantamento dos valores a que têm direito, segundo a agência espanhola EFE.

Até o momento, os pagamentos somaram 2,126 trilhões de guaranis, o equivalente a cerca de US$ 340,4 milhões (R$ 1,87 bilhão) . Ao todo, foram alcançadas 1.738.804 contas cobertas pelo Fundo de Garantia de Depósitos , mecanismo que protege parte do dinheiro dos clientes em caso de problemas financeiros de uma instituição bancária.

A estimativa inicial era de que quase 3 milhões de clientes seriam beneficiados. O número, porém, foi revisto depois que as autoridades excluíram contas sem saldo, registros duplicados e contas com dívidas, entre outras situações, de acordo com a EFE.

O fundo foi acionado após a abertura de um processo de resolução do Ueno Bank, iniciado em razão de problemas de solvência — quando uma instituição financeira não tem condições de cumprir seus compromissos e pagar o que deve.

A crise também teve consequências políticas. Segundo a EFE, Santiago Peña foi destituído da Presidência do país, enquanto Carlos Carvallo renunciou ao comando do Banco Central do Paraguai.

O presidente interino do Paraguai, Pedro Alliana, que assumiu o cargo após o afastamento de Santiago Peña em meio a uma crise política e institucional envolvendo o banco digital Ueno, indicou o economista Jorge Schreiner para comandar o Banco Central do país.

A nomeação ocorre em meio à tentativa de recuperar a confiança no sistema financeiro após o colapso da instituição.

Schreiner já integrou o conselho do Banco Central por dois anos, até 1999, e comandou a Comissão de Valores Mobiliários do Paraguai por uma década, até 2013. Para assumir o cargo, porém, ele ainda precisa receber o aval do Congresso.

Em publicação na rede social X, Alliana afirmou que a indicação busca fortalecer a estrutura institucional do Banco Central e recuperar a confiança da população paraguaia na instituição.

A crise envolvendo o Ueno também provocou mudanças no comando do Banco Central e atingiu o alto escalão político do país. O ex-presidente do Paraguai, Santiago Peña, e o ex-chefe do Banco Central, Carlos Carvallo, foram afastados e passaram a ser investigados por supostos vínculos com o banco. Ambos foram colocados em prisão preventiva.

O colapso da instituição deixou milhões de clientes com dificuldades para acessar suas contas e provocou uma onda de insatisfação social e turbulência política no país.

Além da indicação, Alliana afirmou que recebeu uma ligação do secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio. Segundo o presidente paraguaio, os dois reafirmaram o compromisso de manter a cooperação entre os países.

O economista Jorge Schreiner (à esquerda), o presidente do Paraguai, Pedro Alliana (ao centro), e o ministro da Indústria e Comércio, Marco Riquelme. — Foto: Foto: Reprodução/X via @AllianaPedro

articles.title: Galípolo alerta que a falta de confiança na economia pode manter juros altos no Brasil por anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente do BC afirma que períodos curtos de estabilidade não são suficientes para recuperar a confiança dos investidores e reduzir de forma duradoura os juros de longo prazo.
articles.summary: Presidente do BC afirma que períodos curtos de estabilidade não são suficientes para recuperar a confiança dos investidores e reduzir de forma duradoura os juros de longo prazo.
articles.body:
O presidente do Banco Central (BC), Gabriel Galípolo , afirmou nesta terça-feira (10) que a perda de confiança na economia brasileira pode provocar uma forte desvalorização do real frente ao dólar , com consequências que podem se estender "por muitos anos".

Segundo ele, esse risco ajuda a explicar por que os juros de longo prazo no país permanecem elevados.

Galípolo disse que a percepção de risco dos investidores não está relacionada apenas à capacidade do país de realizar reformas e estabelecer regras, mas também à confiança na economia brasileira.

O chefe do BC participou de um evento promovido pela Associação Brasileira de Câmbio (Abracam), em São Paulo.

"Entre as discussões que a gente faz relativas às taxas de juros mais estruturais e longas no Brasil, pode ser que uma das questões que existam ali também é uma percepção de risco... que talvez esteja relacionada com uma questão de credibilidade, a choques cambiais que decorrem de eventos de perda de credibilidade", afirmou.

O presidente do BC explicou que uma desvalorização do real pode reduzir o retorno dos investidores que compram títulos da dívida pública brasileira, mesmo que esses papéis sejam emitidos predominantemente em moeda nacional.

Isso acontece porque, embora o governo pague a dívida em reais, investidores que avaliam seus ganhos em dólares podem perder dinheiro quando a moeda brasileira se desvaloriza.

Assim, a emissão de títulos em moeda nacional, que é uma vantagem para o governo, representa um risco para quem empresta dinheiro ao país.

"O fato de que a gente emite em moeda doméstica a nossa dívida é uma vantagem para o emissor, mas é um risco para o credor, ele está correndo esse risco de poder ficar mais pobre em dólares se ocorrer um evento de desvalorização", disse.

Galípolo também afirmou que períodos curtos de estabilidade não são suficientes para apagar a percepção de risco provocada por choques anteriores . Segundo ele, os investidores precisam observar um intervalo prolongado sem grandes turbulências para reduzir essa preocupação.

"Períodos tranquilos, se forem curtos, eles não vão conseguir comprimir esse risco, a memória dos choques vai sustentar esse prêmio. Você só vai conseguir uma redução duradoura do risco percebido se você conseguir passar um período longo sem ocorrência de um choque negativo. Credibilidade é construída com o tempo, não vai ter um atalho", afirmou.

O presidente do BC não citou diretamente exemplos recentes nem fez referências ao atual governo.

Falas de Galípolo ecoam em um mercado assutado

As declarações ocorrem em um momento de pressão sobre o mercado financeiro brasileiro. Após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) surpreender ao virar o resultado das eleições no segundo turno contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), o dólar subiu e os juros futuros avançaram .

Na tarde desta terça-feira, as taxas dos contratos de Depósito Interfinanceiro (DI) — usados como referência para os juros esperados pelo mercado nos próximos anos — variavam entre 14% e 15% ao ano para vencimentos de 2028 a 2035 .

Os índices estavam acima da taxa básica de juros, a Selic, atualmente em 13,75% ao ano. O dólar era negociado a R$ 5,58, acima dos cerca de R$ 5 registrados antes do segundo turno.

A pressão sobre os ativos financeiros também ocorre em meio a dúvidas sobre a composição da equipe econômica do quarto mandato de Lula e sobre a política fiscal que será adotada pelo governo.

A política fiscal reúne as decisões sobre gastos e arrecadação do poder público.

Durante a apresentação, Galípolo acrescentou que a parcela da dívida pública brasileira corrigida pela Selic chegou a 51%.

Segundo ele, esse aumento está relacionado à menor disposição dos investidores de assumir riscos em aplicações com prazos mais longos , o que leva o governo a concentrar uma fatia maior de sua dívida em títulos atrelados à taxa básica de juros.

articles.title: Nvidia perde R$ 2,5 trilhões em 2 dias após denúncias de infidelidade e suspeita de espionagem envolvendo CEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação apura relação de Jensen Huang com empresária chinesa suspeita de espionagem; reportagem aponta que vínculo teria facilitado o envio de US$ 7,5 bilhões em chips da fabricante para empresas na China.
articles.summary: Investigação apura relação de Jensen Huang com empresária chinesa suspeita de espionagem.
articles.body:
As ações da Nvidia ampliaram as perdas nesta terça-feira (10) e fecharam em queda de 5,47% . Os papéis eliminaram US$ 470 bilhões (cerca de R$ 2,5 trilhões) em valor de mercado em apenas dois dias.

A queda ocorre em meio à preocupação de investidores com as possíveis consequências de denúncias envolvendo o presidente-executivo da empresa, Jensen Huang , e uma empresária chinesa suspeita de atuar como espiã de Pequim .

Segundo reportagem publicada pelo The Information nesta terça, o relacionamento entre Huang e Alice Huang, que não tem parentesco com o executivo, ajudou a viabilizar o envio de pelo menos US$ 7,5 bilhões (R$ 42 bilhões) em chips da Nvidia para empresas chinesas.

O conselho de administração da Nvidia abriu uma investigação interna no domingo (8).

Nesta terça, os conselheiros independentes anunciaram a contratação de Joon Kim , ex-procurador interino dos Estados Unidos, e do escritório de advocacia Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz para conduzir a apuração.

O FBI, a polícia federal americana, também investiga se Huang, de 63 anos, foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência estrangeira. O executivo já admitiu a funcionários que foi infiel à esposa, mas não deu detalhes sobre o relacionamento.

Na segunda-feira (9), o presidente dos Estados Unidos, D onald Trump, afirmou que conversou com Huang e perguntou se ele sabia que a mulher era suspeita de espionagem para a China . Segundo Trump, o executivo respondeu que não fazia ideia da suposta ligação e que ele acreditava em sua versão.

Trump também disse que desconhecia as suspeitas quando Huang o acompanhou em uma viagem à China, em maio.

No entanto, o New York Times informou nesta terça que o secretário de Estado e conselheiro de Segurança Nacional dos EUA, Marco Rubio , havia comunicado Trump sobre as informações de inteligência que relacionavam Huang a uma mulher suspeita de espionagem chinesa durante o voo presidencial para a China.

De acordo com o jornal, essa foi pelo menos a segunda vez, em sete meses, que Trump recebeu informações sobre as suspeitas. A reportagem cita pessoas com conhecimento do assunto.

As denúncias aumentaram a pressão sobre a Nvidia em relação à transparência de sua administração, ao cumprimento das restrições americanas à exportação de tecnologia e à dependência da empresa da liderança de Huang.

Também ampliaram a preocupação dos investidores sobre os altos gastos com infraestrutura de inteligência artificial e a capacidade de esses investimentos gerarem retorno.

As ações da Nvidia caíram mais de 6% nesta terça , depois de recuarem 4,3% na segunda-feira . Com isso, a Microsoft chegou a ultrapassar brevemente a fabricante de chips e se tornou a segunda empresa mais valiosa do mundo, posição que não ocupava desde junho de 2025.

Em relatório, analistas do Bank of America afirmaram que a principal dúvida dos investidores é se o caso ficará restrito à Nvidia ou se poderá provocar novas restrições e interrupções em toda a cadeia de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial.

Os especialistas ressaltaram, porém, que as acusações não devem ser tratadas como prova de prejuízos aos negócios da companhia.

articles.title: Petróleo cai abaixo de US$ 90 pela primeira vez desde agosto | G1
articles.standfirst: Expectativa de redução das tensões no Oriente Médio diminui temores sobre o fornecimento global de petróleo e pressiona os preços.
articles.summary: Expectativa de redução das tensões no Oriente Médio diminui temores sobre o fornecimento global de petróleo e pressiona os preços.
articles.body:
O preço do barril de petróleo Brent , referência internacional no mercado, caiu abaixo de US$ 90 (R$ 496,31) nesta terça-feira (10), pela primeira vez desde agosto . A queda acontece em meio à expectativa de uma redução das tensões no Oriente Médio, o que diminui o temor de novos problemas no fornecimento global de petróleo.

Durante a manhã, o Brent chegou a US$ 89,66 (R$ 494,44), antes de voltar a ficar pouco acima de US$ 90 (R$ 496,31). Já o petróleo WTI, referência nos Estados Unidos , recuava 2,08%, para US$ 85,04 (R$ 468,96).

🔎 Por que o petróleo importa? O petróleo é matéria-prima para combustíveis e diversos produtos, por isso sua cotação afeta a economia. Quando fica mais caro, pode elevar custos de transporte e produção e pressionar a inflação. No Brasil, a alta também pode aumentar a receita de empresas produtoras e do governo.

A redução da tensão na região ajuda a explicar o movimento. Depois de se reunir com o primeiro-ministro do Catar, Donald Trump afirmou que pretende suspender novos ataques militares contra o Irã, embora os Estados Unidos continuem dispostos a intervir.

Outro fator é a recuperação do transporte de combustíveis. Segundo analistas do ING, os fluxos de petróleo e combustíveis provenientes do Golfo estão próximos dos níveis anteriores à guerra, graças ao uso de rotas alternativas ao Estreito de Ormuz , uma das principais passagens marítimas para o comércio mundial de petróleo.

Apesar disso, ainda não há sinais concretos de que um acordo de paz esteja próximo. Analistas avaliam que o risco de uma nova escalada militar diminuiu, mas a situação continua incerta.

A perspectiva de maior oferta de petróleo também pressiona os preços. O mercado global dá sinais de excesso de oferta, enquanto a produção da Opep aumentou em outubro.

articles.title: Lucro da Petrobras sobe 21,5% no 3º trimestre, para R$ 39,7 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Resultado foi impulsionado por recordes de produção, melhora no desempenho do refino e pela alta do preço do petróleo no mercado internacional.
articles.summary: Resultado foi impulsionado por recordes de produção, melhora no desempenho do refino e pela alta do preço do petróleo no mercado internacional.
articles.body:
Sede da Petrobras, no Rio de Janeiro. — Foto: Fernando Frazão/Agência Brasil

A Petrobras registrou lucro líquido de R$ 39,75 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 21,5% na comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior, informou a companhia nesta terça-feira (10).

A estatal atribuiu o resultado ao forte desempenho operacional. A produção de petróleo bateu recorde pelo terceiro trimestre consecutivo, e a de diesel atingiu seu maior nível histórico. Já as vendas de derivados no mercado interno tiveram o maior volume desde o terceiro trimestre de 2021.

O desempenho também foi favorecido pela valorização do petróleo. Em seu balanço, a Petrobras informou que o preço médio do barril do tipo Brent passou de US$ 69,07 , no terceiro trimestre de 2025, para US$ 97 no mesmo período de 2026, uma alta de 40,4%.

🔎 O petróleo do tipo Brent é a principal referência internacional para a commodity. As cotações dispararam após o início da guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irã, em 28 de fevereiro , com impactos sobre o tráfego no Estreito de Ormuz, uma das principais rotas globais de petróleo .

O diretor Financeiro e de Relacionamento com Investidores da Petrobras , Fernando Melgarejo, afirmou que a performance operacional da empresa contribuiu para uma forte geração de caixa.

"Esses recursos sustentaram os investimentos que estão acelerando a execução dos nossos projetos e antecipando a entrada de nova produção sempre que possível", disse em comunicado

"O fluxo operacional de caixa também assegurou o pagamento de dividendos aos acionistas e contribuiu para a redução da dívida financeira da companhia", acrescentou.

A presidente da Petrobras , Magda Chambriard, destacou os recordes na produção de óleo e gás e o desempenho das refinarias.

"No Refino, alcançamos recorde de produção de diesel e 99% de fator de utilização das refinarias na média deste trimestre, o que foi essencial para garantir a segurança energética do Brasil durante essa crise geopolítica", afirmou.

O Ebitda ajustado da estatal, indicador que mede o desempenho operacional da companhia antes de despesas financeiras, impostos e outros efeitos contábeis, somou R$ 85,82 bilhões entre julho e setembro, alta de 34,3% na comperação anual.

Segundo a Petrobras , foram pagos R$ 90,4 bilhões em tributos à União, estados e municípios entre julho e setembro deste ano.

O conselho de administração da Petrobras também aprovou nesta terça o pagamento de R$ 15,3 bilhões em remuneração para acionistas. O valor equivale a R$ 1,18732774 por ação ordinária e preferencial.

A quantia corresponde a uma antecipação dos pagamentos previstos para o exercício de 2026. O pagamento será feito em duas parcelas, nos meses de fevereiro e março de 2027.

* Com informações da agência de notícias Reuters

articles.title: In 2026, Vande Bharat sleeper trains have been rolled out on three key routes of Delhi-Varanasi, Mumbai-Bengaluru and Guwahati-Howrah; Indian Railways now plans rollout of more rakes
articles.summary: 2026 has been a milestone year for Indian Railways with the introduction of the Vande Bharat sleeper train services.
articles.body: 2026 has been a milestone year for Indian Railways with the introduction of the Vande Bharat sleeper train services. Vande Bharat sleeper trains have been put into service so far on three routes.A few days ago, the Vande Bharat sleeper trains were launched on the Delhi-Varanasi and Mumbai-Bengaluru routes. Earlier this year, the first Vande Bharat sleeper train was introduced between Howrah and Guwahati.Vande Bharat sleeper trains are fully air-conditioned overnight train services that have been designed to offer superior comforts to Rajdhani Express trains, while also reducing travel time with higher average speeds.More Vande Bharat sleeper trains soonIndian Railways has given BEML the contract to manufacture 10 Vande Bharat sleeper trains to begin with. Six out of these have been manufactured and the remaining four are being made.Sources told TOI that two more rakes are expected to be rolled out this month and the other two will be ready in the coming two months.BEML has also been tasked with manufacturing an additional three rakes of Vande Bharat sleeper trains for which the process of procuring the necessary supplies and raw materials has started.Meanwhile, BEML is also manufacturing India’s first high-speed bullet train for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor. A section of this stretch is expected to become operational in the second half of 2027.Vande Bharat Sleeper TrainsDeveloped for long-distance journeys, the Vande Bharat Sleeper aims to bring together modern technology, enhanced safety features and passenger-oriented facilities to improve the experience of travelling overnight. Its design aims to make extended journeys more comfortable, with a focus on sleeping arrangements, hygiene, security, accessibility and convenience.The train can run at speeds of 180 kmph and has been cleared for 160 kmph speeds, though the maximum speed on each route depends on the sectional clearance.Passenger comfort and convenience have also been considered in the design. The train features ergonomically designed, odour-free toilets with vacuum evacuation, along with dedicated berths and toilets for differently-abled passengers.Modern passenger amenities and spacious luggage storage areas are provided to make long journeys more convenient. Integrated BRL units come with a three-pin charging socket and switch, while Type A and Type C USB ports offer additional charging options.In terms of power and performance, the train incorporates regenerative braking to improve energy efficiency, along with an under-slung propulsion system. Its advanced aerodynamic design is intended to support smoother acceleration and deliver a ride with minimal jerks.The train's design features include an austenitic stainless steel car body that meets EN15227 crash standards. It has a fully sealed flexible gangway fitted with a quick-release mechanism, while centrally controlled single-leaf automatic sliding plug doors provide access between the train and its surroundings.Noise insulation and mitigation measures are intended to create quieter passenger saloons. The interiors also feature direct and indirect LED lighting, as well as sensor-based intercommunication doors.Safety and security provisions include compliance with EN45545 HL3-grade fire safety standards and fire barrier doors at the end walls. The train is equipped with a Train Collision Avoidance System (TCAS), disaster management lighting and a smoke and fire detection system (FDS). CCTV cameras support safety and passenger surveillance, while emergency push buttons allow passengers to raise an alarm when required.A PAPIS-based communication system enables interaction among the driver, guard and passengers. First AC passengers have access to showers with hot water. The train also includes a Wi-Fi router with an access point network, while the driver's cab is air-conditioned and crew members have access to a dedicated toilet.Indian Railways has also awarded the contract for manufacturing 50 Vande Bharat sleeper trains with more coaches to ICF. Additionally around 200 Vande Bharat sleeper trains with 16 coaches are being made by Kinet and Titagarh Wagons.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: California's billionaire tax fails, but other 'tax the rich' measures succeeded around the country
articles.summary: The referendum would amend California's constitution and impose a one-time 5% tax on California residents and trusts with assets over $1 billion.
articles.body:
California's proposed billionaire tax went down to defeat, one of the final verdicts from voters in an election that saw a wave of anti-billionaire sentiment elsewhere.

The official call from the Associated Press came nearly a week after election day at 9:28 p.m. ET on Monday and showed California's Proposition 40 down by over 5 percentage points with 83% of the votes counted.

The referendum to amend California's constitution would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on California residents and trusts with assets over $1 billion on Jan. 1, 2026. Some assets, such as real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions, were excluded.

The measure was estimated to impact about 200 billionaires in the state. It faced fierce opposition from many in Big Tech and lost steam with voters as Election Day neared.

Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) co-founder Sergey Brin was one of the most vocal opponents. He contributed a reported $102 million to a political committee to fight the measure.

Other billionaires made detailed plans in case it passed. Meta ( META ) CEO Mark Zuckerberg told his board, according to a New York Times report, that they needed to take steps to shield him from the tax or he would publicly list his home in Palo Alto for sale.

The measure was also opposed by some Democrats, who argued it wouldn't work.

Outgoing California Gov. Gavin Newsom emerged as an opponent, arguing that billionaires would both dodge the tax and leave the state. He cited a report from the California Legislative Analyst's Office that estimated the measure might temporarily boost state revenues but could be an overall drag on regular income taxes and "would reduce state revenues by less than $1 billion per year."

California voters also weighed competing measures: Proposition 41 and Proposition 42 , which were introduced by opponents of Proposition 40 to prevent the wealth tax from taking effect.

Proposition 42 would prohibit taxes on personal savings, assets, and retirement holdings and that measure was ahead on Tuesday with 83% of the votes cast but not yet officially called.

Proposition 41, which aimed to make it harder to pass new special taxes, was defeated.

But proponents of taxes on the rich did have a victory elsewhere on California's ballot.

The state's voters approved Proposition 3, which made permanent higher tax rates on incomes starting at $250,000 in a separate measure that solidified rates first approved in 2012 to fund education.

articles.title: Is the stock market open on Veterans Day?
articles.summary: The New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq are closed for these 10 holidays in 2026 and 2027.
articles.body:

The stock market will be open on Wednesday, Nov. 11, on Veterans Day. The bond market and banks are typically closed this day.

In 2026, the stock market will observe 10 holidays, including two early closings. Many stock market holidays are also federal holidays and banking holidays.

The U.S. stock market's regular hours are 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Eastern time, Monday through Friday. The two major U.S. stock exchanges, the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the Nasdaq, each observe these trading hours. Both stock exchanges are closed on weekends.

You can still place orders to buy and sell stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) during extended trading hours, but there is added risk. The trading volume is lighter after hours, so prices can be more volatile, and your orders may not execute fully.

If you ever find yourself wondering, "Is the stock market open today?" check out this list of stock market holidays for 2026 and 2027.

The NYSE and Nasdaq will observe the following holidays in 2026:

Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, Jan. 19

Washington's Birthday, aka Presidents' Day: Monday, Feb. 16

Juneteenth National Independence Day: Friday, June 19

Independence Day (observed): Friday, July 3

Both stock exchanges will also close at 1 p.m. Eastern time on these days in 2026:

Friday, Nov. 27 (the day after Thanksgiving, aka Black Friday)

In 2027, the NYSE and Nasdaq will observe these holidays:

Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, Jan. 18

Washington's Birthday, aka Presidents' Day: Monday, Feb. 15

Juneteenth National Independence Day (observed): Friday, June 18

Independence Day (observed): Monday, July 5

Christmas Day (observed): Friday, Dec. 24

In 2027, the NYSE and Nasdaq will close at 1 p.m. Eastern time on this day:

Friday, Nov. 26 (the day after Thanksgiving, aka Black Friday)

For holidays that fall on the same date each year, like the Fourth of July and Christmas Day, the stock market is closed the Friday before if the holiday falls on a Saturday or the Monday after if it falls on a Sunday.

One exception: If New Year's Day falls on a Saturday, stock exchanges are open for regular hours the Friday before, and the holiday simply isn't observed by Wall Street.

Most American financial markets also close for a National Day of Mourning upon the death of a past or sitting president. Typically, this day is observed on the day the funeral is held.

The bond market's schedule is determined by the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA). Normal bond market hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern time Monday through Friday.

In 2026 and 2027, bond markets close for all 10 stock market holidays, in addition to Indigenous Peoples Day (formerly known as Columbus Day) in October and Veterans Day in November.

The bond market also closes early at 2 p.m. on the following days:

Thursday before Good Friday (Maundy Thursday)

Friday after Thanksgiving (Black Friday)

Is the stock market closed on the Friday after Thanksgiving?

The stock market is open on the Friday after Thanksgiving, but its trading session closes early at 1 p.m. Eastern time. It's one of two or three days annually that the stock market closes before 4 p.m.

Yes. Unlike the stock and bond markets, the crypto market doesn't observe a holiday schedule because cryptocurrency trades through a decentralized network of computers instead of through central exchanges. You can trade cryptocurrency 24/7/365.

Veterans Day isn't a stock market holiday, as both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq are open for regular hours. However, the bond market does close in observance of Veterans Day.

articles.title: Anthropic sets modest $1 trillion IPO valuation target in a test of Wall Street’s AI fervor
articles.summary: Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion in its landmark U.S. IPO, its filing showed, well short of the ​previously discussed amount.
articles.body: Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion in its landmark U.S. IPO, its filing showed on Tuesday, well short of the ​previously discussed amount in the latest sign of cooling investor appetite for AI. The AI lab and some of its investors are aiming to raise up to $64.4 billion by ‌selling 825 million shares in the IPO in an indicative price band of between $70 and $78 per share. Some prospective investors have questioned whether Anthropic’s previously discussed $1.5 trillion valuation was too high, particularly given the company’s substantial infrastructure commitments and the recent volatility in AI-related stocks. At one point this year, investors expected the IPO to take place in October and to seek a valuation as high as $2 trillion. The company is launching the ​roadshow for a historic share sale that is expected to set a benchmark for the sector, following years of hype that fueled a massive influx of capital into AI companies. Details ​of the blockbuster deal were briefly circulated to investment banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters. The second half of the ⁠year has brought a reckoning for the AI boom, as investors question whether returns will justify the massive spending and mounting debt costs in an elevated interest-rate environment. Concerns are also rising over the sustainability of ​the investment cycle, with questions around circular financing arrangements, the risk of infrastructure overcapacity and how quickly companies can turn their AI investments into revenue. The tech-dominated Nasdaq notched its deepest one-day drop in 19 months ​on Thursday, wiping out trillions in market value on fears of more AI scrutiny, particularly on data center construction, after Democrats’ massive gains in the US midterm elections. Greater oversight and potential regulatory hurdles could complicate the infrastructure buildout underpinning the AI boom. But Anthropic’s growth has so far defied those concerns, propelled by surging demand for its products, particularly its viral Claude models. Its filing spoke of a vision to “bring forth an age of miracles,” even as it warned of existential ​risks to humanity, laying bare the extraordinary promise and profound uncertainties at the heart of the AI boom. Anthropic will also raise $26 billion via a separate private placement deal with cornerstone investors including Alphabet’s ​Google, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. Together with investments from cornerstones, which include Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC, the Anthropic share offering will raise a total of up to $90.4 billion. Certain Anthropic board members and entities affiliated or associated ‌with them ⁠have indicated interest in buying up to $303 million of shares from the offering. Growth and risks Anthropic’s net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47% from a quarter earlier to $16.96 billion, though the pace of growth slowed. It had surged 144% in the prior quarter. The company attributed the breakneck growth to the rapid adoption of Claude, including specialized products targeting industries such as healthcare, financial services and legal services. The prospectus outlined a range of risks facing both the company and the technology, warning that competitors could gain an edge by developing models faster and that advances in AI could outpace Anthropic’s ability ​to put adequate safety and security measures in ​place. The warnings come amid a growing number ⁠of incidents involving “rogue” AI agents that have escaped sandboxed environments and breached private company systems, alongside concerns that increasingly capable AI tools could be used by hackers to penetrate protected networks. Anthropic’s ambitions also come with enormous infrastructure costs. The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet’s ​Google, highlighting how its rapid growth depends on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the ​company’s control. The listing move follows ⁠Elon Musk’s SpaceX, raising $75 billion in the world’s largest IPO in June, at a valuation of nearly $1.75 trillion, excluding additional shares purchased by underwriters through the greenshoe option. Anthropic, locked in a fierce battle for market share with rival OpenAI, was last valued at $965 billion in a private funding round. The company’s prominent investors including Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital. Anthropic, led by CEO Dario Amodei, was founded in 2021 by a group ⁠of researchers who ​left OpenAI following disagreements over governance and AI safety. The shares are expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ​ticker symbol “ANT” after the IPO closes, which would make Anthropic one of the few major companies to go public this fall as higher borrowing costs, geopolitical turmoil and rising bond yields weigh on the IPO market. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading ​the syndicate of investment banks underwriting the offering.

articles.title: Diversifying away from Russia: Trump admin wants to sell Venezuela oil to India, but how much can it buy?
articles.summary: The Donald Trump administration wants India to buy more crude oil from Venezuela.
articles.body: The Donald Trump administration wants India to buy more crude oil from Venezuela. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s recent visit to India to discuss the possibilities with Reliance clearly shows America’s push to increase the market for Venezuelan supplies while encouraging India to diversify away from Russian oil.Russia, however, remains India’s biggest crude oil supplier, having gained a substantial share of the country’s imports after Indian refiners stepped up purchases of discounted Russian barrels. Reliance’s Jamnagar complex can process heavy Venezuelan grades that many refineries cannot easily handle.Rubio has called India a refining superpower. Expanding purchases could give Venezuelan oil a larger market while offering India another source of crude.However, replacing Russian supplies on a significant scale is not straightforward: refinery compatibility, prices, shipping costs and commercial viability will influence whether Indian refiners buy more Venezuelan oil. How much Venezuelan crude can India realistically buy?The difficulty with Venezuelan oilThe biggest problem is that Venezuelan crude oil is not easy to refine.Analysts note that the first problem is its viscosity: Venezuela’s extra-heavy crude needs to be diluted with naphtha or condensate just to move it through pipelines and export it.Then comes the high sulphur content and large residue yield, which require sophisticated refining equipment to turn the oil into valuable fuels.“This is crude that suits complex refineries, but not every refinery can handle it economically,” Natalia Katona, Commodity analyst tells TOI.Quality consistency is another concern, she notes.The crude is high in metals such as vanadium and nickel and in acidity, which poison catalysts and corrode equipment.Naveen Das, Senior Crude Oil Analyst at Kpler says that more than half of each barrel is residue, the thick bottom fraction that must be cracked or coked to make diesel and gasoline.“Only complex refineries with cokers, hydrocrackers and ample hydrogen can earn a margin on it,” he tells TOI.Variations between cargoes, including water content, can make handling and processing more difficult. In some cargoes water content may reach 5%, which adds another operational challenge: buyers need both the equipment and the experience to manage those cargoes.How much can India really buy?According to Kpler data, India imported 4.71 million barrels per day of crude in August and 5.33 million barrels per day in September. Venezuela’s share was 7.4% at the August peak, 3.7% in September and 5.7% in October.“At 450-500 thousand barrels per day on an import base of about 5.2-5.5 million barrels per day, a realistic share is 6-9%. That would match or modestly exceed the 6.7% share recorded in FY18. A share near 10% would need more than 500 thousand barrels per day, which Venezuela’s current export base cannot supply without displacing most non-Indian buyers,” Naveen Das tells TOI.Praveen Rai, Director at Grant Thornton Bharat estimates that India can realistically absorb around 400,000–550,000 barrels per day of Venezuelan crude on a sustained basis, with short-term volumes potentially approaching 600,000 bpd under favourable conditions.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();“Reliance Industries’ Jamnagar complex would remain the principal buyer given its ability to process heavy-sour crude at scale. India has already demonstrated significant absorption capacity, with Venezuelan imports reaching around 444,000 bpd in August 2026,” he tells TOI.Natalia Katona points to another limitation: there will be competition from Gulf countries.“Reliance would do most of the heavy lifting, with IOC another potential buyer, because processing large volumes requires the ability to manage both the residue yield and sulphur. Jamnagar could substitute some Basrah Heavy by Venezuelan crude, but Iraq is much closer. If Iraqi barrels are available at competitive delivered prices, Venezuela has a harder case to make for Indian refiners,” Katona tells TOI.The biggest competitive obstacle is the US Gulf Coast. Its refineries are well suited to Venezuelan crude and much closer to the loading ports.However, the constraint is not simply India’s refining capacity.Venezuela’s production and export availability, shipping economics, sanctions, and the discount of Venezuelan Merey relative to Russian Urals and competing Middle Eastern grades will ultimately determine flows.“Around 500,000 bpd represents a reasonable sustainable level for India, while 550,000–600,000 bpd is achievable during favourable market conditions. Sustaining volumes materially above that level would require higher Venezuelan production and broader participation from Indian refiners beyond Reliance,” Rai says.In this case a natural question would be “can Venezuela simply produce more crude to satisfy both the US and Asian demand”?“I would be cautious about assuming production can quickly reach 2 million b/d (as some market analytics assume). In my view, reaching 1.5 million b/d by 2030 would already be good news,” Katona says.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Does it make economic sense?According to experts, the major question is how much discount as compared to Urals will be available to Indian refineries for processing this crude economically.As Pankaj Srivastava, Senior Vice President, Commodity Market - Oil at Rystad Energy points out: Economics is based upon the configuration and complexity of the refineries and how refineries blend this crude and utilize higher production of coke.In addition to that, how much comparable crude is with Russian Urals as freight, insurance and other changes would play a role in the landed cost of the crude.Also, Indian Refineries are operating at 105-110% utilization rate. Hence, higher portions of Venezuelan crude can hamper the refinery runs.Let’s break this down further:Naveen Das of Kpler is of the view that the oil makes sense for complex refiners, but the margin is narrower than it was.It takes about 40 days via the Cape, and higher tanker rates remain a major risk to long-distance Venezuelan shipments.“The September dip is consistent with that sensitivity. Where the coker margin on the residue plus the discount exceeds freight and the distillate yield penalty, as at Jamnagar, the barrel clears; for simple refiners it does not,” he tells TOI.On the other hand, risks of Russian crude becoming costlier and carrying sanctions risk do improve Venezuela’s relative case.Praveen Rai shares some important insights:Indian customs data for August 2026 show Venezuelan crude, mainly imported by Reliance Industries, landed at 66 dollars per barrel, a 24 dollar per barrel discount to the Indian Crude Basket (ICB) on a delivered basis, compared with 88 dollars for Russian and 93 dollars for Iraqi and Arab Light grades.The headline discount can be eroded by freight since Venezuela is roughly twice as far as Russia and about five times as far as the Middle East!“Industry estimates suggest a discount of about $10-14 per barrel to Brent is needed to offset freight, insurance, and higher processing costs,” he tells TOI.“For complex private refiners, value comes from deep conversion as much as from cheaper feedstock. With most barrels allocated to US refiners and Reliance, and sales governed by US licences and Treasury-controlled accounts, refiners should treat Venezuelan crude as an opportunistic margin boost rather than guaranteed supply,” he cautions.Natalia Katona believes that while it may make some economic sense to buy crude from Venezuela, the freight bill consumes most of the headline discount!Current assessments put Merey at around $36/bbl below ICE Brent on an FOB basis, with $32–34/bbl for VLCC freight to India. That leaves only $2-4/bbl of the discount before insurance, handling and the additional processing costs, she tells TOI.“For such a long voyage, VLCCs provide the necessary scale, as smaller tankers generally make the economics harder. By contrast, Aframax freight from Venezuela to the US Gulf Coast is assessed at around $9-10/bbl. Those shorter voyages can also allow direct delivery and avoid some of the ship-to-ship transfers that larger vessels destined to far away freight require,” she adds.The bottom lineThe clearest case for significantly more Indian buying would be another deterioration in Middle Eastern supply, leaving fewer alternative heavy grades available. Even then, Indian refiners would have to bid competitively against US buyers.Natalia Katona’s view is that this diplomatic significance is larger than the likely increase in physical volumes. articles.title: Anthropic seeks $1.4 trillion valuation in highly anticipated IPO, reportedly aiming for Nov. 19 or Nov. 20 debut
articles.summary: Anthropic seeks $1.4 trillion valuation in latest filing related to its upcoming IPO, which could hit as soon as Nov. 19, according to reports.
articles.body:
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) is seeking a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion in its highly anticipated IPO, setting the stage for one of the largest public-market debuts during the AI boom. The stock is expected to begin trading on Thursday, Nov. 19, or Friday, Nov. 20, of next week, according to the Wall Street Journal .

The AI developer said in an updated filing Tuesday that it plans to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 each. At the top of that range, the IPO would generate up to $64.35 billion in proceeds. On a fully diluted basis, which includes employee stock options and other securities, the frontier AI lab could be valued between roughly $1.3 trillion and $1.45 trillion.

That would mark a substantial increase over the $965 billion valuation that Anthropic announced in a May funding round, but would be far below recent Wall Street estimates, which reached as high as $2 trillion in early October .

On top of the public offering, Anthropic is locking down an extra $26 billion on the side from tech's biggest heavyweights, including Nvidia ( NVDA ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Google ( GOOGL ), TSMC ( TSM) , Broadcom ( AVGO ), AMD ( AMD ), and Micron ( MU ). Those companies are buying nonvoting Class N shares at the same price public investors will pay. Because this is a private deal, those tech giants won't face the standard six-month lockup window that typically prevents insiders from selling right after the debut.

Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

The IPO comes as investors have grown more cautious about the enormous valuations attached to AI companies. Anthropic will also debut against a backdrop of growing political resistance to the build-out of data centers and other infrastructure needed to support AI.

The company's public debut would follow SpaceX's ( SPCX ) record-setting IPO earlier this year. SpaceX raised $85.7 billion in its offering, and the company now has a market capitalization of $1.9 trillion.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei started the company in 2021 alongside a group of former OpenAI researchers. The startup has since emerged as a frontier AI lab and competitor to OpenAI.

Anthropic recently revealed revenue grew $1,206% to $33.2 billion through the first nine months of the year. The company also noted a staggering aggregate committed spend of $895.4 billion , which it said is primarily related to compute and infrastructure.

But the AI growth story was put to the test last week as investors weighed a Democratic congressional win against the impact of the AI data center build-out. The market turmoil prompted prospective buyers to discuss lowering Anthropic's valuation to a range of $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, with some considering as low as $1.1 trillion, according to Bloomberg.

articles.title: Take-Two stock rises on 'unprecedented' preorders for 'Grand Theft Auto VI'
articles.summary: Take-Two Interactive reported earnings after hours on Monday. The studio said preorders for "Grand Theft Auto VI" will deliver "historic" gains.
articles.body:
Investors are revving their engines for the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI." Take-Two Interactive's ( TTWO ) stock was up more than 8% on Tuesday morning despite the video game studio's less-than-stellar Q2 earnings release.

On Monday, the company reported revenue of $1.5 billion for the second quarter, down from $1.77 billion a year prior and missing analyst expectations of $1.65 billion, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.

But traders seem willing to hold tight until Nov. 19. Much of Take-Two's success for the year hinges on what happens over the next two weeks with the eagerly anticipated and much-delayed release of "Grand Theft Auto VI." On Monday, Take-Two said it expects fiscal year 2027 to be "historic."

"Preorders for Grand Theft Auto VI are tracking far in excess of our initial expectations," CEO Strauss H. Zelnick said. "We know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough … with pre-orders continuing to reach unprecedented levels."

Interestingly, that's also what the company said in August on its Q1 earnings call.

While Q2 results showed net bookings down 18%, the company boosted its full-year revenue outlook to between $7.98 billion and $8.18 billion, driven by early success with GTA VI preorders.

The launch of the game was punted twice, first to May 2026 and then to November. The previous iteration, "Grand Theft Auto V," was released in 2013, making this a very long-awaited sequel. For context, the time between GTA IV and V was just over five years.

Following these delays, the stock has whipsawed over the past year, down more than 12% since January.

On Monday, the company reported a second quarter loss of $54 million, or $0.29 per share, and announced that another top game, "NBA 2K27," has sold over 4 million units since its release in September — coming in below expectations. The GTA franchise remains the central driver for Take-Two, with the video game studio leaning on the upcoming launch to offset the softer "NBA 2K27" contribution.

"[GTA VI] promises to be not only highly engaging but in fact, the biggest and most detailed groundbreaking experience Rockstar Games has ever created," Zelnick said. "We believe that fiscal 2027 will be an historic year for Take-Two."

articles.title: Goldman Sachs calls chip stocks 'oversold.' Here are the names it says to buy.
articles.summary: Goldman has found some stocks to buy from within the AI rubble.
articles.body:
Goldman Sachs is sifting through the AI stock rubble in search of bargains.

"We believe stocks are now clearly in oversold territory," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said about semiconductor stocks.

Three of his top names to buy: Nvidia ( NVDA ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), and AMD ( AMD ).

"Even in a 'no growth' scenario for 2028 (which we see as relatively unlikely), NVDA/AVGO are trading 12X/13X this baseline — which we believe valuations are compelling at current levels," Schneider wrote in a note. "We find AMD to be very attractive given the growth we believe it can achieve, albeit at a less compelling valuation."

It has been a brutal run for tech stocks in November.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost 4.3% of its market value on Nov. 5 as investors assessed what a blue wave on Election Day would mean for the build-out of AI data centers. The move wiped out $3 trillion in value.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) plunged 1,800 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ).

Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially semiconductor names.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) is down 21% in the past month, and 6% in November alone.

"We believe the market has been contending with competing tensions relative to semiconductors: (1) How does the funding gap between current capex and free cash flows for hyperscalers and AI model labs levels get closed? (2) Is there sufficient land/power/shell coming on line to match current Street estimates for Semis?" Schneider explained. "Following the US elections on Nov. 3, the second of these tensions came into greater focus with greater uncertainty around the pace of datacenter builds in states such as Texas."

He added, "[Although] we recognize there may be few catalysts for stocks to move higher before year end, we think risk/reward is compelling for select names at current levels."

articles.title: Anthropic says a key AI safety alarm has been triggered, days before its IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic's new IPO filing says AI is now accelerating its own research to the point that it's triggering one of the company's key safety alarms.
articles.body:
A week ago, Anthropic told would-be investors that AI speeding up its own research might "imminently" trigger one of the company's key safety alarms. On Tuesday, in the same filing that set a price range for its record-setting IPO , it said that has now happened.

"We made a determination that we have met this threshold," the company wrote in its amended prospectus . It based the call on "what we expect from future models and our overall rate of progress, rather than on what we have observed from current models."

The safety threshold sits in Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy — the company rulebook for adding tougher safety measures as its AI gets more powerful. This one is triggered when AI is doing enough of Anthropic's research to roughly double how fast its models improve. The policy says that pace would pack two years' worth of AI progress, at its 2018-2024 rate, into a single year. The filing says AI "has already been accelerating our research and development." Crossing the line means more safeguards, not a shutdown.

The fear is AI will improve itself faster than people can check it. In 2023, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei joined other AI leaders in warning that the "risk of extinction from AI" should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.

Anthropic says humans stay in charge. It doesn't expect to safely use Claude "to fully autonomously design and build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision or understanding," the filing says, and it is weighing policy changes "to keep humans in control."

An outside group sees the same speedup. METR, an independent nonprofit that tests AI systems, estimated last week that Anthropic's models have been improving nearly twice as fast since October 2025.

In a separate review , METR called Anthropic's August argument that it was still below the threshold "overstated" and said it was "plausible" the line was crossed by mid-July.

Anthropic set its price range at $70 to $78 per share on Tuesday as it began its roadshow , the round of investor meetings before pricing. That values it at as much as about $1.4 trillion, counting every share that could exist . Trading could start as soon as Nov. 19, according to reports .

Some of the market's biggest names are tied up in the IPO. Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Alphabet's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Google are each buying $10 billion of Anthropic stock at the IPO price, part of a $26 billion private placement with AMD ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), Micron ( MU ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ). Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google already own big stakes.

articles.title: Pepsi sends a shocking memo to employees
articles.summary: The memo went out. Now 125,000 U.S. employees are waiting.
articles.body:
PepsiCo (PEP) North America plans to cut about 1,000 jobs across its North American operations over the next week, according to a Nov. 9 letter to employees from CEO Ram Krishnan, CNBC reported .

The letter described a goal of building what Krishnan called a "stronger, more future-fit business that delivers industry-leading growth." PepsiCo wants to better connect teams across its North American operation, which runs both its beverage and snack businesses.

The memo did not say which roles would be cut. But the timing tells part of the story.

PepsiCo has been struggling with weak demand in the United States and Canada, and the job cuts signal that management has decided the situation calls for more than price adjustments and marketing spending.

Krishnan's letter, as reported by CNBC , did not name the specific roles or divisions that would lose positions. PepsiCo has not issued a public statement beyond what the memo contained. The company employs about 125,000 people in the United States, according to a company filing, and roughly 306,000 globally.

The 1,000 planned cuts are a small share of the global total. But they land squarely on the North American operation, which is the part of the business that has been underperforming. That makes the percentage hit to that specific unit larger than the headline number suggests.

PepsiCo said the restructuring is meant to make the business faster and improve how teams work together. That language points to coordination problems within the North American structure, not just a cost problem.

Why PepsiCo is struggling in North America

In October, PepsiCo lowered its full-year earnings forecast, blaming North America. The third quarter showed the scope of the problem. North American beverage volumes dropped 2%. The food division was flat. Neither business was growing.

CFO Steve Schmitt told analysts on the earnings call that the recovery was taking longer than the company expected, BigGo Finance reported. PepsiCo had already tried cutting prices and spending more on marketing. Neither move produced a sustained volume rebound.

So the company moved to costs instead. Price cuts did not work. Marketing did not work. Now PepsiCo is reorganizing headcount and hoping that gets the job done.

PepsiCo is not alone in cutting roles. This year has seen widespread job reductions across industries, LiveNOW from FOX noted.

Heineken announced up to 6,000 cuts. Nike cut more than 2,000 positions. UPS eliminated up to 30,000 operational roles. Amazon shed roughly 16,000 jobs earlier in the year.

articles.title: Micron stock is a screaming buy at current valuation levels: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: Micron's valuation has reached a level where it's simply too cheap to ignore given its fundamentals, says Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider.
articles.body:
Micron's ( MU ) valuation has reached a level where it's simply too cheap to ignore given its fundamentals, says Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider.

Schneider reiterated his $1,250 price target on the once red-hot AI momentum trade. It assumes about 70% upside from current levels.

"We also believe risk/reward is becoming more attractive for Neutral-rated Micron in light of the high probability of strong free cash flow in the coming quarters," Schneider said.

Micron is currently approaching tangible book value, Schneider noted. When a stock trades below tangible book value, investors value the company at less than the estimated value of its assets after subtracting its liabilities and intangible assets.

In a sense, the market is saying the company's physical and financial assets are worth more than the entire company's stock market value.

That seems to be bordering on an unwarranted disconnect , at least in assessing Schneider's work on the chip player.

Micron's stock is down 17% over the past month amid fears that a blue wave on Election Day could slow the build-out of AI infrastructure. That could have ramifications for orders for Micron's memory chips.

The rout has brought Micron's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio down to an almost laughable 4.2 times, according to Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data. Keep in mind Micron is coming off a quarter of strong demand amid memory chip shortages driving up prices.

The Street still expects Micron to grow earnings by at least 17% in its next fiscal year.

articles.title: They gave redevelopment rights for a 1,395 sq ft flat, but builder withheld Rs 88 lakh compensation and demanded Rs 30.26 lakh; consumer commission orders over Rs 1.22 crore relief to landowners
articles.summary: You give your land for redevelopment to a builder but the latter does not honour his commitment fully, withholds the promised payments, and also fails to
articles.body: You give your land for redevelopment to a builder but the latter does not honour his commitment fully, withholds the promised payments, and also fails to honour other contractual commitments when the flat is handed over to you. What options do you have then?A recent ruling by the Maharashtra Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has addressed this issue, deciding in favour of the landowners.What the case is aboutThe dispute originated in 2010, when two landowners, along with their late mother, transferred their development rights to a builder for redevelopment. They held a one-third undivided share in a property in Mumbai, and executed an Agreement to Assign for the redevelopment.Subsequently, they also entered into a Supplementary Agreement dated February 18, 2015, and an Agreement to Offer Permanent Alternate Accommodation (PAA), executed on the same date.In their complaint before the Consumer Commission, the landowners said that the builder had agreed to allot them a 1,395 sq. ft. flat in the newly constructed building, along with two car parking spaces.The agreement also required the developer to pay monetary compensation, rent for temporary alternative accommodation and a penalty if possession was delayed.In addition, the builder was responsible for executing and registering the agreement and bearing the stamp duty and registration charges for up to 1,000 sq. ft. of the allotted area.The landowners received physical possession of the flat in May 2018. However, according to an ET report quoting their complaint, the developer neither paid its agreed share of the stamp duty nor executed the registered PAA Agreement.They also alleged that the builder had not paid the enhanced compensation of Rs 88 lakh for the increased floor space index (FSI), as stipulated in the Supplementary Agreement.Other outstanding amounts included Rs 6,60,000 towards rent for temporary accommodation for the period from December 2017 to April 2018, Rs 16,50,000 as a penalty for delayed possession, and Rs 10,00,000 to reimburse the cost of raw materials they had purchased.Instead of meeting these commitments, the landowners claimed, the developer sent them a “baseless legal notice” in June 2022, demanding Rs 30,26,592 towards alleged construction expenses.Why did the Consumer Commission rule in favour of the landowners?Legal experts point out that the landowners were able to establish their entitlements because these had been explicitly documented in agreements executed between the parties.The developer's failure to honour contractual commitments that were clearly set out in these documents was another important factor in the outcome, Bhargav KS, Managing Partner at K.S & B.K.S Law Associates, Bengaluru, told ET.The agreements specified the landowners' rights to alternative accommodation, enhanced FSI compensation, rent during the transit period, compensation for delayed possession and registration. Their affidavits and correspondence provided evidence of the developer's defaults, while the fact that possession was handed over only in May 2018 helped establish the delay in delivery.The Commission also recognised that surrendering development rights amounted to consideration for “housing services”.The Commission noted that the developer had obtained the benefits of the development rights and handed over possession of the flat in May 2018, but had failed to complete a key statutory requirement.The Commission reportedly said, "the developer blatantly ignored the statutory mandate of the Maharashtra Ownership Flats Act, 1963, by failing to register the Agreement to Offer Permanent Alternate Accommodation,".It also found that the builder had withheld financial benefits legitimately due to the landowners. The Commission observed that the demand notices seeking Rs 30,26,592 from the landowners amounted to a clear instance of an unfair trade practice.According to the Commission, the developer's actions reflected a serious and deliberate failure to discharge both its contractual commitments and statutory responsibilities.The matter was heard ex parte against the developer, which did not appear despite receiving notice.The Commission consequently directed the builder to execute and register the Agreement to Offer Permanent Alternate Accommodation within 60 days of receiving the order. It also instructed the developer to bear the stamp duty and registration charges for up to 1,000 sq. ft. of carpet area.The builder was further ordered to pay Rs 88 lakh as compensation for enhanced FSI, with interest at 8% from the date of default until the amount is actually recovered by the landowners. The directions also included payment of Rs 6,60,000 towards outstanding rent for temporary accommodation and Rs 16,50,000 as a penalty for delayed possession, the ET report said.In addition, the developer must reimburse Rs 10,00,000 for the raw materials purchased by the landowners. The Commission awarded a further Rs 1,00,000 as compensation for mental agony, harassment and hardship, along with Rs 50,000 towards litigation expenses.Taken together, the directions require the builder to pay the landowners more than Rs 1.22 crore, besides complying with the order to execute and register the permanent alternate accommodation agreement.You use AI every day.
